overview_description.description: The African Export Import Bank (the “Bank”) was created by the African government, African private and institutional investors as well as non-African financial institutions and private investors for financing, promoting, and expanding intra-African and extra-African trade. The Bank was established under the twin constitutive instruments of an Agreement signed by member States and multilateral organizations, and which confers on the Bank the status of an international multilateral organization; as well as a Charter, governing its corporate structure and operations, signed by all Shareholders.

about_short_description.short_description: The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) focuses on financing, promoting, and expanding intra-African and extra-African trade.

product.name: Trade Finance
product.description: Financing solutions that support intra-African and extra-African trade, including working capital and structured funding for exporters, importers, banks and governments.

product.name: Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS)
product.description: A payment and settlement infrastructure for cross-border African trade that enables participating banks and businesses to process eligible transactions using African currencies.

product.name: Trade and Project Finance
product.description: Loans and structured financing for trade-related projects, infrastructure and productive assets that expand African industrial capacity and regional commerce.

product.name: Trade Guarantees and Risk Mitigation
product.description: Guarantees and other risk-mitigation instruments that help banks and businesses manage payment, performance and cross-border trade risks.

product.name: Africa Trade Gateway (ATG)
product.description: A digital trade platform that provides infrastructure and services intended to facilitate cross-border commerce and access to African trade markets.

product.name: AfCFTA Adjustment Fund
product.description: A US$10 billion financing facility established to help countries and eligible businesses adjust to and participate effectively in the African Continental Free Trade Area.
